A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MLHCA research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite pagination changes and additions in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original learning experiments and auction simulations across GSVM, LSVM, SRVM, and MRVM, including efficiency, revenue, and bridge-bid analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds the Inverse query-order experiment in Appendix G.9.

M1.justification: Appendix F substantially revises Algorithm 5's specified VQ procedure. v2 retrains each round and generates fresh bidder-specific marginal queries; v3 trains at the beginning of a block, precomputes queries with individual bidders excluded, and serves them through a FIFO queue without further training or optimization. It also excludes pending queries when constructing the batch. Experimental reruns are not established.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same four SATS domains and spectrum-allocation tasks. The new Inverse experiment evaluates a different mechanism configuration on three existing domains, without adding data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Inverse as an evaluated comparator in Table 11 and Figure 6. The existing BOCA, ML-CCA, CCA, and extended Table 9 comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: Appendix G.9 adds an 80-VQ/20-DQ comparison against MLHCA's 40-DQ/60-VQ configuration using matched instances and hyperparameters. Table 8 corrects SRVM local bidders from 1000 hidden units and 10 epochs to 10 units and 1000 epochs. Table 9 changes MVNN, NN, FT, and RS query counts from 100 DQs to 100 VQs; Table 5 corrects its second HPO criterion from Vr to Vp. These reported corrections do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: Appendix G.9 adds a focused ablation of query ordering, comparing final efficiency and convergence trajectories against Inverse in GSVM, LSVM, and SRVM. The existing mixed-query learning and bridge-bid analyses are retained.

E5.justification: The existing run and seed information, 95% confidence intervals, and t-tests at the 5% significance level are retained. The new Inverse experiment follows the existing practice of reporting auction curves over 50 instances with confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Table 11 adds Inverse results, including LSVM efficiency loss of 5.12 ± 2.18% versus MLHCA's 0.04 ± 0.07%. The SRVM difference is not statistically significant, and Figure 6 reports no efficiency improvement from Inverse's final DQ phase. Existing learning, benchmark, and revenue scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Theorem 3.2/D.11 strengthens the 55% impossibility statement to 50% plus arbitrarily small epsilon, adding a parametric proof covering infinitely many instances. Proposition C.5 also corrects the predicted demand optimizer from argmin to argmax and repairs its scaling inequality. These are substantive mathematical revisions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same hybrid-auction novelty, learning advantages, efficiency improvements, and query-reduction claims. The added query-order experiment supplies further support without redefining these headline contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendices D.4–D.5 explicitly acknowledge that cognitive load was not measured and qualify the supporting practitioner intuition. Remarks G.1–G.2 explain SRVM's early VQ advantage and the preprocessing difference from BOCA. Appendix B.4 additionally clarifies that the detection guarantee concerns inconsistent reports, not all strategic misreports.

D1.justification: v3 adds code-access information in the abstract and Appendix G, corrects the reported SRVM configuration, and documents queue handling and empty-bundle responses in Appendix F. Appendix G.9 explains the SRVM representation difference from BOCA. Hardware, SATS version, and overall runtime disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Appendix A.1 adds d'Eon et al. (2024) and Almahdi et al. (2025) on reinforcement learning for bidder strategies. Appendix D.5 adds a substantive discussion of the already-cited Scheffel experiment's applicability to real auctions. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: v3 corrects typos and cross-references, adds acknowledgments and publication information, expands Appendix F's explanation, and introduces explanatory subsections D.4–D.5 and G.9. These are focused extensions within the retained document structure.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 11 and Figure 6, revises Algorithm 5's display, and relocates existing figures and tables. Figure 3(a)'s caption changes from 60 demand queries to 60 value queries, matching the existing experiment description. The retained plot graphics are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v3 improves precision through the generalized impossibility proof, mathematical and configuration corrections, and code-access information. The new experiment adds useful evidence about query sequencing, while the cognitive-load qualification improves transparency. The gains are limited: existing benchmark results remain unchanged, and the new ablation omits MRVM and changes query proportions as well as order, so it does not isolate ordering alone.
